fixes.explanation: Joshua says it was the LORD their God who fought for them. His words are “…it was the LORD your God who fought for you.” (Joshua 23:3) Later he says, “One of you can put a thousand to flight, because the LORD your God fights for you…” (Joshua 23:10) Whenever Israel won, the LORD was the one fighting, so he's the one to thank.

That's it, baker! The LORD drives the nations out so Israel can take possession of their land, and Joshua says it's “…as the LORD your God promised you.” (Joshua 23:5) Driving out, taking over and a promise, all packed into one verse. That's a well-packed cookie box.

Rebuilding is a good word, but it isn't in this verse. Joshua says the LORD will push those nations out and drive them out so Israel can take possession of their land (Joshua 23:5). The word for the blank is possess. If I rebuilt something every time I got nervous, my bakery would be nothing but sawdust.

Eleazar doesn't show up anywhere in this speech. Joshua names who to hold fast to: “…the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.” (Joshua 23:8) The name sounds official, so it's an easy one to grab. But the text keeps it simple, and the answer is the LORD.

Borders sound sensible, but that's not what Joshua says to watch. He says, “Therefore watch yourselves carefully, that you love the LORD your God.” (Joshua 23:11) The watching is aimed at themselves, not at a fence. I'll admit a fence is easier to inspect than a heart.

Yes. Joshua says those nations will become “…a snare and a trap, a scourge in your sides and thorns in your eyes…” (Joshua 23:13) A snare and a trap catch you, and a scourge and thorns hurt. That's four pictures in one verse, and not one of them is comfortable.

Joshua doesn't paint it that way. He says they will become “…a snare and a trap, a scourge in your sides and thorns in your eyes…” (Joshua 23:13) Nobody is working a field in that picture. It's all traps and thorns.

Yes, the answer is False. Joshua says, “…not one of the good promises the LORD your God made to you has failed. Everything was fulfilled for you; not one promise has failed.” (Joshua 23:14) He says it two ways, back to back. He also says they know it with all their heart and soul.

Joshua says both halves. “…just as every good thing the LORD your God promised you has come to pass, likewise the LORD will bring upon you the calamity He has threatened…” (Joshua 23:15) I think this is a heavy verse. The good promises came to pass, and Joshua says the threatened calamity will too.

That's what Joshua says. “If you transgress the covenant of the LORD your God, which He commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them, then the anger of the LORD will burn against you…” (Joshua 23:16) It's a serious verse. The cause is named plainly: breaking the covenant, serving other gods and bowing down to them.
